newsitem.title: USA: Fujimori to meet Clinton at White House.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori to meet Clinton at White House.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori will meet U.S. President Bill Clinton at the White House on Monday, a Peruvian embassy official told reporters.
The Peruvian leader is extending his stay in Washington until Tuesday, the official said, instead of returning to Lima Monday evening.
An early morning meeting with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright was cancelled, the State Department said. She will attend the White House meeting with Clinton, the Peruvian official said.

Fujimori was originally scheduled to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, and not the president, at an early-morning meeting but that was cancelled. She will attend the White House meeting with Clinton, the Peruvian official said.

Fujimori arrived in Washington on Saturday from Toronto, where he held an emergency summit with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to discuss what to do about rebels holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

The two leaders agreed to push for direct talks with the rebels, who have held the Japanese residence since Dec. 17., but ruled out the guerrillas' demand for the liberation of about 400 MRTA members jailed in Peru.

Fujimori said on Saturday he was optimistic about talks because the rebels had "implicitly" given ground on their main demand. But the international spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels said Fujimori's interpretation that release of jailed comrades was no longer a key demand was incorrect.
